content: @Kim Morrison @François G. Dorais It looks like batteries#1736 broke Mathlib (in that currently the commit it introduces is the only one on top of Mathlib's current commit and the Mathlib checks failed). This is now causing all batteries PRs based on an up-to-date main to fail mathlib integration.
The alternative is that this simply didn't build for the same reason the others are failing - BUT we are getting String-related errors in Mathlib. It does look to me like this PR has introduced them.
Yae:l and I believe we have identified the issue: see batteries#1748.
OK - I think this WILL fix the Mathlib build issue, but there is still an issue with the CI - something is breaking pre-build. This is happening now across multiple PRs.

Yes, there's something wrong with the CI. I've been running the Mathlib test locally. Unfortunately, that introduces risks of human error. I suspect that's what happened. I'll have a look and probably just undo that commit.
I think 1748 ought to fix it but yeah it's a Mystery
Oh, I fixed this in Mathlib's nightly testing already, I thought it was easy.
The CI problem?
No, the String incompatibility
Yes I mean it didn't take long - the main issue is that it got merged at all despite at the time causing a Mathlib break, because CI isn't working.
Ah, yes, sorry I had already fixed the set_option ... in problem in nightly-testing, but forgot to port it back to main.

Yes. Again I just felt somewhat annoyed to be somewhat lightly yelled at/encouraged to make Mathlib work for that other PR when in fact what needed to happen was not that and you had already broken it.
Is nightly testing CI working again?
Do you mean testing Mathlib against Batteries PRs?
(that's separate from nightly-testing)
Oh sorry - yes, it uses the nightly testing fork is what I meant
Though I assumed it was all the same CI for that fork.

It seems right now it is unfixable, as Batteries is already on v4.30.0-rc1 and Mathlib is still on v4.29.0. We'll have to wait until Joscha gets further through the release of v4.30.0-rc1 before this is repairable.
batteries#1750 now integrates the above change btw, I think FGD felt it was better to revert and integrate
Ah, I see François' comment at https://github.com/leanprover-community/batteries/pull/1750#issuecomment-4169790299. This is the thing I fixed on Mathlib's nightly-testing.
Hmm. It does somewhat feel an issue that a library on which Mathlib depends can advance version in this way, breaking downstream, given we have specific checks in place to fix things downstream.
Yes.
Currently it feels like we're navigating without a compass. Even if we're not getting lost it still makes me nervous!

Obviously it's necessary that Batteries advances toolchains before Mathlib does. This can't happen atomically. Usually I get these done within about a 1 hour window, but this cycle we have a new release manager (Joscha Mennicken) and it's a bit more spread out as he learns the system.
Oh that makes sense
Well if it's in aid of getting new people up to speed that is understandable
But I think it should mean that batteries PRs need to provide hard evidence of manual Mathlib fixes in the meantime.

I've looked at the Mathlib Testing issue but I couldn't figure out what's going wrong. It fails at the first cache step on every CI. If it helps, LEAN_SRC_PATH is incorrect but I don't understand why that would matter at this stage.

Because manual testing leads to human errors as we have just seen, I will not be merging anything until this is fixed.
I think that is (sadly) the right call.
